title: Strings & Runes
description: Learn about string constants, runes, string manipulation, and formatting in Go
theory:
## Strings in Go

Strings in Go are immutable sequences of bytes (usually UTF-8).

### String Basics

```go
str := "Hello, World!"
fmt.Println(len(str))        // 13 bytes
fmt.Println(str[0])          // 72 (byte, not character)
```

### Runes (Unicode Code Points)

A rune is Go's term for a Unicode code point:
```go
ch := 'A'          // rune literal
r := rune('中')     // Chinese character

fmt.Printf("%c", ch)  // Print as character
fmt.Printf("%d", ch)  // Print as code point (65)
```

### Converting String to Runes

```go
str := "hello"
runes := []rune(str)  // Convert to []rune
bytes := []byte(str)  // Convert to []byte
```

### The strings Package

```go
import "strings"

strings.Contains(s, "ell")     // true
strings.Replace(s, "l", "x", 1)  // "hexlo" (first only)
strings.Replace(s, "l", "x", -1) // "hexxo" (all)
strings.Split(s, "l")           // ["he", "", "o"]
strings.Join([]string{"a","b"}, "-")  // "a-b"
strings.ToUpper(s)
strings.ToLower(s)
strings.TrimSpace(s)
strings.HasPrefix(s, "he")
strings.HasSuffix(s, "lo")
```

### String Formatting

```go
// Sprintf - returns string
s := fmt.Sprintf("%s is %d years old", "Alice", 30)

// Printf - prints to stdout
fmt.Printf("Pi: %.2f\n", 3.14159)

// Common verbs:
// %s - string
// %d - integer
// %f, %.2f - float, float with 2 decimals
// %c - character/rune
// %v - any value
// %T - type
```

### String Indexing

Strings are byte-indexed, not character-indexed (important for non-ASCII):
```go
s := "héllo"
s[0] // 'h' (first byte of 'h')
s[1] // 'é' (first byte of 'é', which is 2 bytes in UTF-8)
```
For proper Unicode iteration, use runes or for-range.

exercises.title: String Constants
exercises.description: Declare a string variable greeting and assign it the value "Hello, Go!". Then print it using fmt.Println.
hints: Use greeting := "Hello, Go!" to declare and assign

exercises.title: Using Runes
exercises.description: Declare a rune variable and assign it the Unicode character for 'A'. Print it using both %c and %d verbs to see character vs code point.
hints: Use var ch rune = 'A' or ch := 'A'
Use fmt.Printf("Character: %c\n", ch) for the character
Use fmt.Printf("Code Point: %d\n", ch) for the Unicode code point
exercises.solution:
package main

import "fmt"


func main() {
    ch := 'A'
    fmt.Printf("Character: %c\n", ch)
    fmt.Printf("Code Point: %d\n", ch)
}

exercises.title: String Manipulation
exercises.description: Use strings.Contains to check if "Hello" is in "Hello, World!", strings.Replace to replace "World" with "Go", and strings.Split to split "a,b,c" by comma.
exercises.expected_output:
Contains: true
Replaced: Hello, Go!
First: a

exercises.title: String Formatting
exercises.description: Use fmt.Sprintf to format a string with a name and age, then print it. Also use fmt.Printf to format a floating point number to 2 decimal places.
exercises.expected_output:
Alice is 30 years old
Pi is 3.14
hints: fmt.Sprintf("%s is %d years old", name, age) creates the formatted string
Use fmt.Printf("Pi is %.2f\n", pi) for 2 decimal places
exercises.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    name := "Alice"
    age := 30
    
    s := fmt.Sprintf("%s is %d years old", name, age)
    fmt.Println(s)
    
    pi := 3.14159
    fmt.Printf("Pi is %.2f\n", pi)
}
